title: One Big Prompt vs Chunked Prompts

blocks.content: Course: Rapid Build With Claude Code
One Big Prompt vs Chunked Prompts
The most common mistake I see when people start using Claude Code is treating it like a genie: write one giant prompt, describe the entire app, and expect a working product. This does not work.
A one-big-prompt approach fails for three predictable reasons:

items: Context overload - Claude Code loses track of earlier requirements as the prompt gets longer
No checkpoints - If something goes wrong, you have no safe point to roll back to
Untestable output - You cannot verify a half-built app; you have to wait until the end to see if it works

blocks.content: Chunked prompts solve all three. Each chunk is a focused unit of work with a clear scope, testable output, and a git commit at the end. If Chunk 4 breaks something, you roll back to the Chunk 3 commit and try again. The build never moves forward from a broken state.

For SpeedBlip, the entire application was broken into 7 chunks before a single one was written. That pre-planning meant each chunk had clear boundaries and I knew exactly what I would test after each one ran.

blocks.alt: Left side: single giant arrow from Prompt to App with a question mark over the output. Right side: seven numbered arrows, each ending with a checkmark and git commit badge
